capsuleTopic.title: Sacrifice
capsuleTopic.subtitle: Gift · altar · blood · meal · atonement · self-giving
capsuleTopic.orientation: Trace sacrifice as Scripture names and reshapes it: gifts and meals, animal and grain offerings, covenant blood, cleansing rites, prophetic protest, Jesus’ self-giving, and lives offered in response.
capsuleTopic.trailPrompt: Follow who brings the gift, what is given, where it goes, who receives or eats it, and what the source says the act does.

passages.observation: Manasseh rebuilds high places, erects Baal and Asherah worship, builds heavenly-host altars in the temple courts, and makes his son pass through fire.

passages.title: Josiah removes rival worship and restores Passover
passages.excerpt: The king commanded Hilkiah the high priest, and the priests of the second order, and the keepers of the threshold, to bring out of the LORD’s temple all the vessels that were made for Baal, for the Asherah,…
passages.observation: Josiah destroys vessels, priests, high places, child-sacrifice sites, horses, altars, and images, then commands a Passover unmatched since the judges.

passages.title: Fire and glory answer the temple dedication
passages.excerpt: Now when Solomon had finished praying, fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices; and the LORD’s glory filled the house.  The priests could not enter into the LORD’s house…
passages.observation: Fire consumes the offerings, glory fills the house, the people bow and give thanks, and Solomon and Israel dedicate the temple with abundant sacrifice and feast.

passages.title: Hezekiah restores temple sacrifice and song
passages.excerpt: Then Hezekiah the king arose early, gathered the princes of the city, and went up to the LORD’s house.  They brought seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven male goats, for a sin offering for the kin…
passages.observation: Leaders bring sin offerings, priests apply blood, musicians resume Davidic song, the assembly bows, and abundant offerings exceed priestly capacity.

passages.title: Josiah’s Passover mobilizes priests, Levites, and gifts
passages.excerpt: Josiah kept a Passover to the LORD in Jerusalem. They killed the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.  He set the priests in their offices and encouraged them in the service of the LORD’s house…
passages.observation: Josiah provides animals, assigns priestly and Levitical service, restores music, and celebrates a Passover said to be unlike those since Samuel.

passages.title: The altar stands before the temple is rebuilt
passages.excerpt: When the seventh month had come, and the children of Israel were in the cities, the people gathered themselves together as one man to Jerusalem.  Then Jeshua the son of Jozadak stood up with his brothers the…
passages.observation: Returned exiles build the altar despite fear, restore continual and festival offerings, and gather materials while the temple foundation is not yet laid.

passages.title: Job offers for what his children may have done
passages.excerpt: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job. That man was blameless and upright, and one who feared God, and turned away from evil.  There were born to him seven sons and three daughters.  His poss…
passages.observation: Job regularly offers burnt offerings for each child after their feasts, reasoning that they may have sinned in their hearts.

passages.title: Opened ears stand beside unwanted sacrifice
passages.excerpt: I waited patiently for the LORD. He turned to me, and heard my cry.  He brought me up also out of a horrible pit, out of the miry clay. He set my feet on a rock, and gave me a firm place to stand.  He has pu…
passages.observation: The speaker recalls rescue, says sacrifice was not desired but ears were opened, and delights to do God’s will and proclaim righteousness.

passages.title: God rejects the idea that he needs Israel’s animals
passages.excerpt: “Hear, my people, and I will speak. Israel, I will testify against you. I am God, your God.  I don’t rebuke you for your sacrifices. Your burnt offerings are continually before me.  I have no need for a bull…
passages.observation: God says every creature is already his, calls for thanksgiving and fulfilled vows, and rebukes those who recite covenant while practicing evil.

passages.title: A broken spirit comes before restored sacrifices
passages.excerpt: Deliver me from the guilt of bloodshed, O God, the God of my salvation. My tongue will sing aloud of your righteousness.  Lord, open my lips. My mouth will declare your praise.  For you don’t delight in sacr…
passages.observation: The speaker asks for deliverance, says God does not delight in sacrifice alone, names a broken spirit, and then anticipates righteous offerings in restored Zion.

passages.title: Thanksgiving asks how to repay deliverance
passages.excerpt: What will I give to the LORD for all his benefits toward me?  I will take the cup of salvation, and call on the LORD’s name.  I will pay my vows to the LORD, yes, in the presence of all his people.  Precious…
passages.observation: The speaker lifts the cup of salvation, calls on the LORD, fulfills vows, brings thanksgiving sacrifice, and does so publicly in Jerusalem.

passages.title: Prayer is set before God like incense
passages.excerpt: LORD, I have called on you. Come to me quickly! Listen to my voice when I call to you.  Let my prayer be set before you like incense; the lifting up of my hands like the evening sacrifice.  Set a watch, LORD…
passages.observation: The speaker asks for a quick hearing, compares prayer with incense and lifted hands with evening sacrifice, and asks for guarded speech and desire.

passages.title: Justice is more acceptable than sacrifice
passages.excerpt: The king’s heart is in the LORD’s hand like the watercourses. He turns it wherever he desires.  Every way of a man is right in his own eyes, but the LORD weighs the hearts.  To do righteousness and justice i…
passages.observation: The proverb places the king’s heart under the LORD, notes that people see their own ways as right, and says righteousness and justice are more acceptable than sacrifice.

passages.title: Many offerings cannot cover violent hands
passages.excerpt: Hear the LORD’s word, you rulers of Sodom! Listen to the law of our God, you people of Gomorrah!  “What are the multitude of your sacrifices to me?”, says the LORD. “I have had enough of the burnt offerings…
passages.observation: The LORD rejects multiplied sacrifices, incense, festivals, and prayer while hands are full of blood, then calls for washing, justice, and willing obedience.

passages.title: The servant bears sin and gives his life
passages.excerpt: Surely he has borne our sickness and carried our suffering; yet we considered him plagued, struck by God, and afflicted.  But he was pierced for our transgressions. He was crushed for our iniquities. The pun…
passages.observation: The servant is wounded, bears iniquity, is led like a lamb, makes his life an offering for sin, and intercedes for transgressors.

passages.title: Foreigners’ offerings are accepted in the house of prayer
passages.excerpt: The LORD says: “Maintain justice and do what is right, for my salvation is near and my righteousness will soon be revealed.  Blessed is the man who does this, and the son of man who holds it fast; who keeps…
passages.observation: Those formerly excluded who hold fast the covenant receive a place and name, and foreigners’ offerings are accepted on God’s altar.

passages.title: Chosen offerings can become acts of violence
passages.excerpt: The LORD says: “Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool. What kind of house will you build to me? Where will I rest?  For my hand has made all these things, and so all these things came to be,” sa…
passages.observation: The LORD contrasts heaven and earth with a human-built house, regards the humble, and compares unchosen sacrifice with murder, broken necks, blood, and idolatry.

passages.title: Temple confidence meets the command to obey
passages.excerpt: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying,  “Stand in the gate of the LORD’s house, and proclaim this word there, and say, ‘Hear the LORD’s word, all you of Judah, who enter in at these gates to w…
passages.observation: Jeremiah confronts worshipers who trust the temple while oppressing and shedding blood; God recalls that the exodus command centered on hearing his voice.

passages.title: Topheth exposes child sacrifice as uncommanded
passages.excerpt: Thus said the LORD, “Go, and buy a potter’s earthen container, and take some of the elders of the people and of the elders of the priests;  and go out to the valley of the son of Hinnom, which is by the entr…
passages.observation: Jeremiah breaks a jar in the valley and announces judgment because Judah burned children there, an act God says he did not command or imagine.

passages.title: Polluted gifts include firstborn children
passages.excerpt: Moreover I swore to them in the wilderness, that I would scatter them among the nations and disperse them through the countries,  because they had not executed my ordinances, but had rejected my statutes, an…
passages.observation: Ezekiel recalls wilderness rebellion, says Israel polluted itself through gifts by making firstborn pass through fire, and rejects the desire to worship like the nations.

passages.title: A future altar is measured and purified
passages.excerpt: “These are the measurements of the altar by cubits (the cubit is a cubit and a hand width): the bottom shall be a cubit, and the width a cubit, and its border around its edge a span; and this shall be the ba…
passages.observation: Ezekiel receives precise altar dimensions and a seven-day purification rite before offerings are accepted on the eighth day.

passages.title: An anointed one and the end of sacrifice enter the vision
passages.excerpt: While I was speaking, praying, and confessing my sin and the sin of my people Israel, and presenting my supplication before the LORD my God for the holy mountain of my God—  yes, while I was speaking in pray…
passages.observation: While Daniel prays, Gabriel speaks of seventy weeks, an anointed one cut off, a destroyed city, covenant, and sacrifice and offering ceasing midway through a week.

passages.title: Loyal love is desired more than sacrifice
passages.excerpt: “Come! Let’s return to the LORD; for he has torn us to pieces, and he will heal us; he has injured us, and he will bind up our wounds.  After two days he will revive us. On the third day he will raise us up,…
passages.observation: Israel speaks of returning and expects swift healing, but the LORD compares its loyalty to morning mist and desires covenant love and knowledge over offerings.

passages.title: Songs and offerings are rejected without justice
passages.excerpt: “Woe to you who desire the day of the LORD! Why do you long for the day of the LORD? It is darkness, and not light.  As if a man fled from a lion, and a bear met him; or he went into the house and leaned his…
passages.observation: Amos overturns longing for the LORD’s day, rejects festivals and offerings, refuses songs, and calls for justice to roll like water.

passages.title: Sailors sacrifice after the sea becomes calm
passages.excerpt: Then they said to him, “What shall we do to you, that the sea may be calm to us?” For the sea grew more and more stormy.  He said to them, “Take me up, and throw me into the sea. Then the sea will be calm fo…
passages.observation: The sailors reluctantly throw Jonah into the sea at his instruction, the storm stops, and they fear the LORD, offer a sacrifice, and make vows.

passages.title: Escalating gifts give way to a stated requirement
passages.excerpt: How shall I come before the LORD, and bow myself before the exalted God? Shall I come before him with burnt offerings, with calves a year old?  Will the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams? With tens of t…
passages.observation: The speaker imagines offerings rising from calves to thousands of animals to a firstborn child, while the answer names justice, mercy, and humble walking.

passages.title: Defective animals expose contempt at the altar
passages.excerpt: “A son honors his father, and a servant his master. If I am a father, then where is my honor? And if I am a master, where is the respect due me?” says the LORD of Armies to you priests who despise my name. “…
passages.observation: Priests offer blind and injured animals, question how they despise God’s name, and are contrasted with a great name among the nations.

passages.title: Unjust wealth makes an offering unclean
passages.excerpt: He who sacrifices a thing wrongfully gotten, his offering is made in mockery. The mockeries of wicked men are not acceptable.  The Most High has no pleasure in the offerings of the ungodly, Neither is he pac…
passages.observation: Sirach compares sacrifice from wrongful gain with mockery and murder, says the Most High rejects the lawless, and joins prayer with ending injustice.

passages.title: Keeping the law is described as abundant offering
passages.excerpt: He who keeps the law multiplies offerings. He who heeds the commandments sacrifices a peace offering.  He who returns a kindness offers fine flour. He who gives alms sacrifices a thank offering.  To depart f…
passages.observation: Sirach names obedience, kindness, almsgiving, and leaving wickedness as offerings, while still commanding gifts to the altar without bribery.

passages.title: Imperial sacrifice desecrates the altar
passages.excerpt: King Antiochus wrote to his whole kingdom that all should be one people,  and that each should forsake his own laws. All the nations agreed according to the word of the king.  Many of Israel consented to his…
passages.observation: The king orders one people and foreign worship, builds an abomination on the altar, burns incense, suppresses Scripture, and executes those who resist.

passages.title: The defiled altar is dismantled and rededicated
passages.excerpt: But Judas and his kindred said, “Behold, our enemies are defeated. Let’s go up to cleanse the holy place and to rededicate it.”  All the army was gathered together, and they went up to mount Zion.  They saw…
passages.observation: Judas and his brothers cleanse the sanctuary, store defiled stones, build a new uncut-stone altar, restore furnishings, offer sacrifice, and establish a dedication festival.

passages.title: A collection funds a sin offering for the dead
passages.excerpt: Judas gathered his army and came to the city of Adullam. As the seventh day was coming on, they purified themselves according to the custom, and kept the Sabbath there.  On the following day, when it had bec…
passages.observation: After idols are found on fallen soldiers, Judas collects money for Jerusalem, acts with resurrection hope, and provides a sin offering for the dead.

passages.title: Martyr blood is described as ransom and purification
passages.excerpt: The tyrant himself, and all their council, admired their endurance,  through which, they also now stand beside the divine throne and live a blessed life.  For Moses says, “All the saints are under your hands…
passages.observation: The writer says the faithful martyrs became a ransom for the nation, their blood and death purified Israel, and the tyrant was punished.

passages.title: Reconciliation interrupts an altar gift
passages.excerpt: “You have heard that it was said to the ancient ones, ‘You shall not murder;’ and ‘Whoever murders will be in danger of the judgment.’  But I tell you that everyone who is angry with his brother without a ca…
passages.observation: Jesus places anger and insult under judgment and tells a worshiper remembering a broken relationship to leave the gift, reconcile, and then return.

passages.title: Mercy, not sacrifice, answers table criticism
passages.excerpt: As Jesus passed by from there, he saw a man called Matthew sitting at the tax collection office. He said to him, “Follow me.” He got up and followed him.  As he sat in the house, behold, many tax collectors…
passages.observation: When Pharisees question Jesus eating with tax collectors and sinners, he names the sick, calls for learning mercy, and states his mission to call sinners.

passages.title: Bread and cup are named body and covenant blood
passages.excerpt: As they were eating, Jesus took bread, gave thanks for it, and broke it. He gave to the disciples and said, “Take, eat; this is my body.”  He took the cup, gave thanks, and gave to them, saying, “All of you…
passages.observation: At the meal Jesus gives bread and cup, names them as his body and covenant blood poured out for forgiveness, and looks toward drinking anew in the kingdom.

passages.title: Jesus dies and the temple curtain tears
passages.excerpt: As they came out, they found a man of Cyrene, Simon by name, and they compelled him to go with them, that he might carry his cross.  When they came to a place called “Golgotha”, that is to say, “The place of…
passages.observation: Jesus is crucified, mocked, cries out, dies, the curtain tears, the earth shakes, tombs open, and the centurion responds.

passages.title: The Son of Man gives his life as a ransom
passages.excerpt: James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came near to him, saying, “Teacher, we want you to do for us whatever we will ask.”  He said to them, “What do you want me to do for you?”  They said to him, “Grant to us…
passages.observation: Jesus answers a request for status by naming service, suffering, and the Son of Man’s mission to give his life as a ransom for many.

passages.title: The cup is covenant blood poured out for many
passages.excerpt: As they were eating, Jesus took bread, and when he had blessed it, he broke it and gave to them, and said, “Take, eat. This is my body.”  He took the cup, and when he had given thanks, he gave to them. They…
passages.observation: At the meal Jesus gives bread and cup, names body and covenant blood poured out for many, and looks toward drinking new wine in God’s kingdom.

passages.title: The centurion responds when Jesus dies
passages.excerpt: When the sixth hour had come, there was darkness over the whole land until the ninth hour.  At the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, “Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani?” which is, being interprete…
passages.observation: Darkness covers the land, Jesus cries out and dies, the temple veil tears, and the centurion names him God’s Son.

passages.title: Jesus’ family brings the poor family’s offering
passages.excerpt: When eight days were fulfilled for the circumcision of the child, his name was called Jesus, which was given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.  When the days of their purification according t…
passages.observation: Mary and Joseph present Jesus, bring the pair of birds named in the law, and hear Simeon and Anna speak about salvation, opposition, and redemption.

passages.title: Passover, kingdom, body, cup, and betrayal share one table
passages.excerpt: When the hour had come, he sat down with the twelve apostles.  He said to them, “I have earnestly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer,  for I tell you, I will no longer by any means eat of…
passages.observation: Jesus desires to eat Passover before suffering, points toward kingdom fulfillment, gives bread and cup as body and new-covenant blood, and names the betrayer’s hand.

passages.title: Jesus dies after pardon, mockery, and entrusted spirit
passages.excerpt: There were also others, two criminals, led with him to be put to death.  When they came to the place that is called “The Skull”, they crucified him there with the criminals, one on the right and the other on…
passages.observation: Jesus is crucified with two criminals, speaks pardon, promises Paradise, darkness falls, the curtain tears, and he entrusts his spirit before death.

passages.title: John identifies Jesus as God’s Lamb
passages.excerpt: This is John’s testimony, when the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him, “Who are you?”  He declared, and didn’t deny, but he declared, “I am not the Christ.”  They asked him, “What then?…
passages.observation: John denies being the Christ, describes his baptismal witness, and points to Jesus as the Lamb of God who takes away the world’s sin.

passages.title: Jesus disrupts the temple market and names his body
passages.excerpt: The Passover of the Jews was at hand, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.  He found in the temple those who sold oxen, sheep, and doves, and the changers of money sitting.  He made a whip of cords and drove all…
passages.observation: Jesus drives sellers and animals from the temple, rejects making his Father’s house a market, and answers with a saying about destroying and raising the temple of his body.

passages.title: The good shepherd lays down his life
passages.excerpt: “I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.  He who is a hired hand, and not a shepherd, who doesn’t own the sheep, sees the wolf coming, leaves the sheep, and flees. The wol…
passages.observation: Jesus contrasts the good shepherd with a hired hand, says he lays down his life for the sheep, and speaks of authority to lay it down and take it again.

passages.title: Jesus dies as Passover preparation continues
passages.excerpt: So then he delivered him to them to be crucified. So they took Jesus and led him away.  He went out, bearing his cross, to the place called “The Place of a Skull”, which is called in Hebrew, “Golgotha”,  whe…
passages.observation: Jesus is crucified during Passover preparation, his garment and thirst sayings fulfill Scripture, his bones remain unbroken, and blood and water flow from his side.

passages.title: The apostles stop a pagan sacrifice
passages.excerpt: At Lystra a certain man sat, impotent in his feet, a cripple from his mother’s womb, who never had walked.  He was listening to Paul speaking, who, fastening eyes on him and seeing that he had faith to be ma…
passages.observation: After a healing, the crowd calls Barnabas and Paul gods and brings bulls and garlands; the apostles tear their clothes and redirect the people to the living Creator.

passages.title: Gentile believers receive a blood and idol-food boundary
passages.excerpt: Therefore my judgment is that we don’t trouble those from among the Gentiles who turn to God,  but that we write to them that they abstain from the pollution of idols, from sexual immorality, from what is st…
passages.observation: The Jerusalem letter does not impose circumcision but asks Gentile believers to abstain from idol pollution, sexual immorality, strangled animals, and blood.

passages.title: Paul joins a temple purification offering
passages.excerpt: When we had come to Jerusalem, the brothers received us gladly.  The day following, Paul went in with us to James; and all the elders were present.  When he had greeted them, he reported one by one the thing…
passages.observation: To answer reports about his teaching, Paul joins four men under a vow, pays their expenses, and enters the temple until the offering is made.

passages.title: God presents Christ as an atoning sacrifice
passages.excerpt: But now apart from the law, a righteousness of God has been revealed, being testified by the law and the prophets;  even the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ to all and on all those who bel…
passages.observation: Paul says God’s righteousness is revealed through faith in Jesus Christ, all have sinned, and God presents Christ through his blood to demonstrate righteousness.

passages.title: God condemns sin in the likeness of sinful flesh
passages.excerpt: There is therefore now no condemnation to those who are in Christ Jesus, who don’t walk according to the flesh, but according to the Spirit.  For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus made me free fr…
passages.observation: Paul says there is no condemnation in Christ because God sent his Son in the likeness of sinful flesh and for sin, condemning sin in the flesh.

passages.title: Living bodies become a reasonable sacrifice
passages.excerpt: Therefore I urge you, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, which is your spiritual service.  Don’t be conformed to this world, but be transform…
passages.observation: Paul appeals for bodies to be presented as a living, holy, acceptable sacrifice and for minds to be transformed rather than conformed.

passages.title: Paul describes Gentile mission as priestly offering
passages.excerpt: I myself am also persuaded about you, my brothers, that you yourselves are full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, able also to admonish others.  But I write the more boldly to you in part as reminding…
passages.observation: Paul describes grace for priestly service of the gospel so the Gentiles may become an acceptable offering sanctified by the Holy Spirit.

passages.title: Christ our Passover is sacrificed
passages.excerpt: Your boasting is not good. Don’t you know that a little yeast leavens the whole lump?  Purge out the old yeast, that you may be a new lump, even as you are unleavened. For indeed Christ, our Passover, has be…
passages.observation: Paul uses leaven and festival language to address tolerated wrongdoing, names Christ as the sacrificed Passover, and calls for sincerity and truth.

passages.title: Knowledge yields to another person’s conscience
passages.excerpt: Now about things sacrificed to idols: We know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.  But if anyone thinks that he knows anything, he doesn’t yet know as he ought to know.…
passages.observation: Paul says an idol is nothing and God is one, yet warns that eating in an idol temple can wound a weak conscience and become sin against Christ.

passages.title: The Lord’s table excludes participation at demon tables
passages.excerpt: Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.  I speak as to wise men. Judge what I say.  The cup of blessing which we bless, isn’t it a sharing of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, isn’t it a shar…
passages.observation: Paul joins cup and bread with participation in Christ, recalls Israel’s altar, and warns that pagan sacrifices involve demons rather than God.

passages.title: The Lord’s supper is distorted by unequal eating
passages.excerpt: But in giving you this command I don’t praise you, because you come together not for the better but for the worse.  For first of all, when you come together in the assembly, I hear that divisions exist among…
passages.observation: Paul rebukes divisions and humiliation of the poor, repeats the bread-and-cup tradition, and calls for self-examination and discernment.

passages.title: Aroma language describes apostolic witness
passages.excerpt: Now when I came to Troas for the Good News of Christ, and when a door was opened to me in the Lord,  I had no relief for my spirit, because I didn’t find Titus my brother, but taking my leave of them, I went…
passages.observation: Paul thanks God for leading the apostles and spreading knowledge through them as Christ’s aroma, received as life by some and death by others.

passages.title: One dies for all and reconciliation is entrusted
passages.excerpt: For the love of Christ compels us; because we judge thus: that one died for all, therefore all died.  He died for all, that those who live should no longer live to themselves, but to him who for their sakes…
passages.observation: Christ’s love controls Paul because one died for all; God reconciles the world in Christ and entrusts the message of reconciliation to ambassadors.

passages.title: The Son of God loved and gave himself
passages.excerpt: “We, being Jews by nature and not Gentile sinners,  yet knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law but through faith in Jesus Christ, even we believed in Christ Jesus, that we might be justi…
passages.observation: Paul says a person is justified through faith in Jesus Christ, has been crucified with Christ, and now lives by faith in the Son who loved and gave himself.

passages.title: Christ gives himself as offering and aroma
passages.excerpt: Be therefore imitators of God, as beloved children.  Walk in love, even as Christ also loved us and gave himself up for us, an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweet-smelling fragrance.
passages.observation: Believers are called to walk in love because Christ loved and gave himself for them as an offering and sacrifice to God, a fragrant aroma.

passages.title: Paul’s life is poured over their faith
passages.excerpt: Do all things without complaining and arguing,  that you may become blameless and harmless, children of God without defect in the middle of a crooked and perverse generation, among whom you are seen as light…
passages.observation: Paul calls for blameless witness and holds out the word of life, then describes being poured out on the sacrifice and service of the believers’ faith.

passages.title: A financial gift becomes fragrant sacrifice
passages.excerpt: But I rejoice in the Lord greatly that now at length you have revived your thought for me; in which you did indeed take thought, but you lacked opportunity.  Not that I speak because of lack, for I have lear…
passages.observation: Paul receives the Philippians’ renewed support, says he has learned contentment, and calls their gifts a fragrant, acceptable sacrifice pleasing to God.

passages.title: Peace is made through the blood of the cross
passages.excerpt: He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation.  For by him all things were created in the heavens and on the earth, visible things and invisible things, whether thrones or dominions or…
passages.observation: The hymn names Christ as image, creator, head, beginning, and fullness, then says God reconciles all things through the blood of his cross.

passages.title: The one mediator gives himself as ransom for all
passages.excerpt: I exhort therefore, first of all, that petitions, prayers, intercessions, and givings of thanks be made for all men,  for kings and all who are in high places, that we may lead a tranquil and quiet life in a…
passages.observation: Prayer is urged for all people because God desires salvation; the one mediator, Christ Jesus, gives himself as ransom for all at the proper time.

passages.title: Paul says he is already being poured out
passages.excerpt: For I am already being offered, and the time of my departure has come.  I have fought the good fight. I have finished the course. I have kept the faith.  From now on, the crown of righteousness is stored up…
passages.observation: Facing departure, Paul describes himself as a drink offering, remembers the finished race and kept faith, and awaits the righteous Judge’s crown.

passages.title: A different priesthood is argued from Melchizedek
passages.excerpt: For this Melchizedek, king of Salem, priest of God Most High, who met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him,  to whom also Abraham divided a tenth part of all (being first, by int…
passages.observation: Hebrews reads Melchizedek, blessing, tithes, oath, and endless life to contrast Levitical succession with Jesus’ permanent priesthood.

passages.title: A heavenly ministry and new covenant are set together
passages.excerpt: Now in the things which we are saying, the main point is this: we have such a high priest, who sat down on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens,  a servant of the sanctuary and of the t…
passages.observation: Hebrews names Jesus as high priest in the true tent, distinguishes earthly copies, and quotes Jeremiah’s promise of a new covenant written on hearts.

passages.title: Sanctuary blood is contrasted with Christ’s own blood
passages.excerpt: Now indeed even the first covenant had ordinances of divine service and an earthly sanctuary.  For a tabernacle was prepared. In the first part were the lamp stand, the table, and the show bread, which is ca…
passages.observation: Hebrews surveys the first tent and annual entry, then presents Christ entering the greater tent with his own blood to cleanse conscience and mediate covenant.

passages.title: Repeated offerings are set beside one offered body
passages.excerpt: For the law, having a shadow of the good to come, not the very image of the things, can never with the same sacrifices year by year, which they offer continually, make perfect those who draw near.  Or else w…
passages.observation: The law’s repeated sacrifices cannot perfect worshipers; Psalm language is applied to Christ’s body, whose one offering opens a new way and ends repeated sin offerings.

passages.title: Abraham offers Isaac in the memory of faith
